messages:
Samir: Hey team — Peregrine (new customer) sent a short security questionnaire as part of onboarding. They have three quick items we should answer today: 1) logging retention & PII redaction policy, 2) who can access raw logs and what approval flow is, 3) list of subprocessors + KMS/encryption detail. Link in thread. Can someone draft suggested answers so I can return by EOD?

Ava: I can start. Suggested short answers below — keep them customer-facing and non-opsec. Will flag anything that needs legal review.

Ava: 1) Retention: default 90 days, longer retention can be arranged via contract. PII redaction: we redact known patterns at ingestion and scrub sensitive fields before indexing. Example short wording: "Logs are retained for 90 days by default. PII is redacted at ingestion using deterministic scrubbing (emails, credit-card patterns, SSNs) and structured fields containing sensitive customer data are never stored. Longer retention available under contract."

Ava: 2) Access: access to raw logs is limited to oncall SRE and Platform Engineering for troubleshooting, and to Security for investigations. Access requests follow an approval flow and are logged/audited. Example: "Raw log access requires an approved ticket scoped with timeframe and justification; approvals are granted by the SRE manager and recorded in audit logs."

Jordan: +1 for that wording. Quick clarifications on implementation: our ELK/Graylog stack has role-based access with read-only vs read-write roles. We also have an access-review process every 90 days.

Jordan: I'll add: "Role-based access controls (RBAC) enforced via our logging platform. Access reviews are performed quarterly; all access is logged."

Nadia: For PII redaction detail, we run both regex-based scrubbing and a minimal-postprocessing pipeline that strips known sensitive headers before storage. Config snippet (internal) below — don't share verbatim but useful for internal answer: 
```
log_redact:
  enabled: true
  patterns:
    - email:
        regex: /[a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}/
    - cc:
        regex: /(?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?)/
  drop_sensitive_fields: ["credit_card", "ssn"]
  retention_days: 90
```

Evan: For the subprocessors list — customer wants names + locations. We can share an approved vendor list (names + primary service + region). Legal needs to OK sharing contracts or detailed SLA items.

Mike: We can share the vendor register (names and country/region) and whether they are subprocessors for production data. Do not attach contracts. I can sign off on the vendor list; send me the compiled list and I'll confirm.

security-bot: SOC2 status: InScope: Logging & Monitoring, Access Controls. Last attestation: 2025-02-10. Audit evidence path: /confluence/soc2/2025-evidence (internal).

Ava: For KMS/encryption: short answer: "All customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256; encryption keys are managed in customer-specific KMS where requested (customer-managed keys for Private deployments) and in our managed KMS for hosted. Access to keys is strictly limited and audited."

Samir: Great. Two quick asks before I send: 1) Jordan — confirm the exact retention number and whether we need to mention the quarterly review; 2) Evan/Mike — compile the vendor register as a single CSV and attach to the response.

Jordan: Confirmed retention = 90 days default. We do quarterly reviews; include that.

Evan: I'll produce the CSV and paste it into the ticket. Will mark any vendors that are in-scope for production data.

Mike: Fine to share CSV with customer. Please redact contract-specific pricing or SLAs.

Samir: Perfect — I'll assemble the final response (concise) and post it to the customer. Draft to send back: 

Samir: "Thanks — see answers below:
1) Retention & redaction: Logs retained 90 days by default. PII is redacted at ingestion using pattern-based scrubbing and sensitive structured fields are not stored. Longer retention available under contract.
2) Access & approvals: Raw log access is limited to SRE, Platform, and Security teams for troubleshooting and investigations. Access is role-based, requires a scoped approval ticket, and is recorded in audit logs. Access reviews occur quarterly.
3) Subprocessors & encryption: We will provide the list of subprocessors (name + region). Production data is encrypted at rest with AES-256; for Private deployments customers can use customer-managed keys.

If you require copies of contracts or more granular audit artifacts we can arrange an NDA and legal review."

Ava: Looks good to me. :thumbsup:

Jordan: LGTM.

Evan: I'll upload the CSV to the ticket now.

Mike: Approved to send.

Samir: Thanks all — sending now and filing the update in the SOC2 evidence folder. Closing loop.

Evan: (uploaded) vendor_register_peregrine.csv attached to ticket #ONB-412.

Samir: Thanks — noted.

Nadia: If you want I can add a short internal note to eng docs about the redaction pipeline so the Customer Success docs stay accurate.

Samir: Yes please do that, Nadia — ticketing me the PR when ready.

security-bot: Reminder: any shared vendor lists with customers should be recorded in the vendor-share log.

Samir: Will do. Closing thread.
